scope: Source-reference admission per image after actual visual inspection and game/platform/costume review. It does not rewrite any older combat-admission flags or qualify an animation. No global promotion of port/candidate sources.

references.sourceVariantLabel: Zombie1 — green/grey vest, dark trousers, short brown hair
references.observation: Actual512px front/left/right source renders inspected. The unarmed source body, both outstretched arms/hands in front view, torso clothing, full trousers and dark footwear are inside the frames. Side views confirm body depth. This is a sourceTpose, not a combat idle.
references.basis: Published source catalog explicitly maps this Zombie model to Resident Evil0/GameCube2002, the target game/release. The R33 hold records pose/action/appui qualification, not a port/year discrepancy. RawCapcompackage equivalence and exact native lighting remain uncertified.
limits: A complete view set supports this exact costume only; the blonde/red-shirt catalogue costume is not qualified by these models.
Reference admission does not admit the Tpose to combat or certify original game pixels.

references.sourceEdition: Unresolved edition of the retained purple/horned Mutated Steve render
references.reason: The retained purple/horned render differs from the human brown-haired face and green body in the Code: Veronica gameplay capture. The render edition is not established; no positive Darkside or other-edition attribution is claimed. New admission and retained presentation fallbacks are held pending exact source proof.
references.observation: Actually opened the 450x360 catalogue crop, complete 500x425 same-render source and Code: Veronica gameplay screenshot. The catalogue is the same purple/horned render as the complete source, with a different face/body appearance from the supplied gameplay view.
references.basis: The secondary page labels Code: Veronica, but a separate article by its image supplier describes using improved Chronicles renders for earlier games. This raises an unresolved source-edition conflict; the label alone cannot qualify the target incarnation.
limits: This holds the R34 default presentation without modifying historical R33 files or claiming a positively identified alternative game.
The actual generated portrait remains preserved as GENERATED but is not admitted; these records do not create any new image.
